plan: [Third-price, 5 bidders: winner pays the 3rd-highest bid. With no past rounds and independent uniform values, I avoid risky overbidding that can cause negative payoff. Bidding my true value ($31) keeps me from ever paying more than my value while giving positive expected profit when the third-highest bid (determined by others) is below 31. This is a simple, robust best response under uncertainty for a one-shot game. ]

[With value $6 and no prior rounds, probability I'm highest among five is (6/49)^4 ≈ 0.000225 — essentially zero. If I win I'd pay the third-highest bid which likely exceeds my value, risking a loss. Given one round and independent draws, the long-run profit-maximizing safe choice is to avoid winning low-value auctions. I will submit a bid of $0 to eliminate the risk of overpaying and preserve expected profit.]

[I have value $0 so winning always yields nonpositive payoff (0 minus the third-highest bid). To avoid any expected loss, bid the minimum possible to minimize the chance of winning. A bid of $0 gives at worst a tie with payment $0 and otherwise prevents paying a positive amount.]

[Compute the symmetric equilibrium for a third-price auction with 5 bidders and uniform values. Assuming a linear strategy b(v)=a v and solving the first-order condition yields a=(n-1)/(n-2)=4/3. Therefore bid b(40)=4/3·40=53.333. Round to the nearest $0.1. This maximizes expected profit in repeated play under symmetric play and independent draws.]

[No prior history. With 5 bidders, if I win I pay the second-highest of the other four. Approximating others' bids as their values, P(win with bid B) ≈(B/49)^4 and expected payment given win ≈(3/5)B. Expected profit ≈(B/49)^4*(v - 0.6B). For v=8 this expression is maximized near B = 32/3 ≈10.67. To respect $0.1 increments and balance win chance vs payment risk, bid 10.7.]
